STH infection is negatively associated with concurrent viral infection, but positively associated with concurrent bacterial and protozoan infection.
STH infection is associated with lower odds for concurrent viral infection but higher odds for concurrent bacterial and protozoan infection.
soil-transmitted helmins were negatively associated with concurrent viral infection but positively associated with concurrent bacterial and protozoan infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of STH infection and preventive chemotherapy on concurrent microparasitic infection in Laos.
the effect of S. japonicum and other soil-transmitted helmins on concurrent viral, bacteria and protozoan infections.
the interactions between STH, viral, bacterial, protozoal, and helminth enteropathogens.

the association between STH infection and concurrent microparsite infections may reflect reverse causality.
STH infection is associated with concurrent microparasites infections, but the direction of this effect is not consistent across microparasite taxonomic group.

the effect of S. japonicum infection on concurrent enteric infections may differ by pathogen type, whereby S. japonicum was negatively associated with enteric virus infection but positively associated with enteric bacterial and protozoan infections, and that the impact of concurrent S. japonicum infections on concurrent enteric pathogen co-infections requires further study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is an association between STH and enteric microparaste infections.
the impact of STH infection may differ by micoparasite taxa, and may be a double-edged sword for the human host.
the effect of S. stercoralis infection on concurrent microparasites was different from other helminths.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immunomodulation of helminths is not a one size fits all phenomenon, but instead is likely to have different effects on different pathogens.
STH infection may affect concurrent enteric micoparasite infections, and that these effects are likely complex and may differ by pathogen taxa.
there is a need to better understand the complex interplay between STH and enteric pathogens.
